title: Where Things Go
overview: Say where places are: behind, between, in front of. Say where you go: I walk to the bank. Say what you use: I cut it with a knife. Say how a person feels: I'm tired. I feel happy. Read a note on a door, and do what it says.
learningPath: Words: listen, look and say. 25 words.
Patterns: 3 cards. Read the one done for you.
Reading: a busy day, a guide and a note.
Speaking: tap the mic. Say it. Listen.
Writing: a street and a made-up day.
Practice: write. Check with the answers.
lectureScript:
Hello! This is Unit 12.
In this unit, you say where things are and where they go.
Three people are at a bus stop: Eva, Dan and Zoe.
Eva is first. Eva is in front of Dan.
Zoe is last. Zoe is behind Dan.
Dan is between Eva and Zoe.
In front of is three words. Say them together: in front of.
Between: one on each side. Say the two with and.
Now a street in a town.
The café is between the bank and the chemist.
A taxi is in front of the café.
The cinema is behind the café. You cannot see it from the street.
Now, where do you go? Use to.
I walk to the corner.
She goes to the library.
To: you are going there. At: you are there.
I go to the bank. Now I am at the bank.
Not: I go at the bank. Say: I go to the bank.
Now, the things you use.
I cut the bread with a knife. Now it is in two parts.
I use a knife. With: the thing you use.
I wash my hands with soap.
My hands are wet. I dry them with a towel.
I clean the floor with a brush.
He fixes the bike with a tool.
You know with a friend: together.
And you know for: the person who gets it.
This present is for you.
I cut the paper with scissors. I make a card for my sister.
Scissors is one thing, but say are: The scissors are on the desk.
Now, how do you feel?
Say I'm and a feeling word.
I'm tired. I want to sleep.
I'm hungry. I want to eat.
I'm thirsty. I want to drink.
Or say I feel. I feel happy. He feels sad.
Use one, not both.
Not: I'm feel tired. Say: I feel tired.
Not: I have hungry. Say: I'm hungry.
Cold: not hot. I'm cold. Please close the window.
Afraid comes with of. She is afraid of the water.
Ask: How do you feel? How are you?
Now say the town words. Listen and repeat.
bank, market, corner.
HOS-pi-tal. Hospital.
Chemist starts like key. Chemist.
Cinema starts like city. Cinema.
library, post office, café, building.
In Speaking 4, you hear new words.
Listen to the words around a new word. They help you.
In Reading, there is a note on a door.
It says where to go on Saturday. Read it and do what it says.
Now go to Words. Goodbye!

outcomes.outcome: Say where a place, a thing or a person is, with behind, between and in front of.
outcomes.evidence: Pattern 1 practice self-checked; Practice 1, eight items; Speaking 1 and 6 recordings; Writing 1 checklist; Quiz items 1 to 3.
outcomes.cefrDescriptor: I can say: The café is between the bank and the chemist.

outcomes.outcome: Ask the way to a place in a town, and give it with walk to and go to.
outcomes.evidence: Practice 2, eight items; Speaking 2 recording; Writing 4 checklist; Quiz items 4 and 5.
outcomes.cefrDescriptor: I can ask: Where is the bank, please? I can say: Walk to the corner.

outcomes.outcome: Write what you use with with, and who gets a thing with for: I cut it with a knife. It is for you.
outcomes.evidence: Pattern 2 practice; Practices 3 and 4; Speaking 3 recording; Writing 2 checklist; Quiz items 6 to 8.
outcomes.cefrDescriptor: I can write: I cut it with a knife. It is for you.

outcomes.outcome: Say, with a model, how a person feels, with I'm, is and feel.
outcomes.evidence: Pattern 3 practice; Practice 5, eight items; Speaking 5 recording; Quiz items 9 and 10.
outcomes.cefrDescriptor: I can say how a person feels: She is tired.

outcomes.outcome: Write short lines about how people feel on a made-up day, and join two ideas with and.
outcomes.cefrDescriptor: I can write how people feel on a made-up day.

outcomes.outcome: Follow a short talk about where to go, and work out a new word from the words around it.
outcomes.evidence: Speaking 4: the talk, its four answers and the key; Quiz item 11.
outcomes.cefrDescriptor: I can work out a new word from the words around it.

outcomes.outcome: Read a short guide, a sign and a notice, and follow what they say to do.
outcomes.evidence: Reading 2 questions 6 and 7; Reading 3 questions 8 to 10; Practice 6; Quiz item 12.
outcomes.cefrDescriptor: I can read a notice and do what it says.

words.meaning: You feel good. Your day is good.
words.example: I'm happy. My friend is here.
practice: Mia is happy today.
I feel happy in the park.
Are you happy with your new phone?
We are happy. The film is good.
words.tutor: Tell the tutor about a made-up good day in three lines, and end with I feel happy. Ask it to check you said I feel, not I'm feel.

words.meaning: Not happy. You feel bad.
words.example: I'm sad. I lost my watch.
practice: He is sad. He lost his key.
The film is sad.
Don't be sad. We can find it.
I feel sad at the end of the book.
words.tutor: Ask the tutor for a short made-up story about a person. Say if the person is happy or sad, and say the line from the story that tells you.

words.meaning: You want to sleep.
words.example: I'm tired. I worked all day.
practice: She is tired at night.
Are you tired? Sit here.
We are tired. We walked to the city.
I feel tired in the evening.
words.tutor: Say three lines about a made-up busy day, then end with I'm tired. Ask the tutor to check each past word, like worked or walked.

words.meaning: You want to eat.
words.example: I'm hungry. Can I have some bread?
practice: Are you hungry? There is rice in the kitchen.
The baby is hungry.
We are hungry. The café is near.
He is hungry. He didn't eat today.
words.tutor: Tell the tutor you are hungry in a made-up café. Ask for two things with Can I have …, please? and answer its questions.

words.meaning: You want to drink.
words.example: I'm thirsty. Can I have some water?
practice: She is thirsty. She drinks a glass of milk.
Are you thirsty? Here is some tea.
It is hot, and we are thirsty.
The man at the market is thirsty.
words.tutor: Say thirsty and Thursday to the tutor in any order. Ask it which word it heard each time. They start the same, so say the ends clearly.

words.meaning: You feel very bad about a thing a person did.
words.example: He is angry. A man took his bike.
practice: The driver is angry. A car stopped in front of his bus.
Don't be angry. It is OK.
Are you angry? No, I'm not. I'm tired.
My neighbour is angry. The music is very loud.
words.tutor: Ask the tutor for three short made-up problems, like A car stopped in front of your bus. Say angry, sad or worried for each one.

words.meaning: You feel a bad thing can happen soon.
words.example: Dan is worried. His bus is late.
practice: I'm worried. I can't find my key.
She is worried about her mother.
Don't be worried. The bus is here.
The shopkeeper is worried. There is no bread today.
words.tutor: Worried ends in -ed but has only two parts: WOR-ried. Say it to the tutor and ask it to check you did not say worri-ed.

words.meaning: A bad thing is near you. You want to run away.
words.example: He is afraid of the water. He can't swim.
practice: Are you afraid of planes?
Don't be afraid. I am here.
The child is afraid at night.
He is not afraid. He can swim well.
words.tutor: Afraid comes with of: afraid of the water. Ask the tutor for five things, and say a line with afraid of or not afraid of for each one.

words.meaning: Not hot. You want a hot drink.
words.example: I'm cold. Please close the window.
practice: It is cold today.
Are you cold? Have a hot tea.
The water is cold.
We are cold at the bus stop.
words.tutor: Say I'm cold, then ask the tutor for two things you can say next, like Please close the door. Say each one back.

words.meaning: A place. People keep their money there.
words.example: The bank is between the café and the chemist.
practice: I go to the bank on Friday.
Is there a bank near here?
The bank opens at nine o'clock.
Two people are in front of the bank.
words.tutor: Ask the tutor Is there a bank near here? Let it answer with a made-up street, then say its answer back: The bank is …

words.meaning: A place with many tables of fruit, vegetables and fish. You pay at each table.
words.example: I get fruit at the market.
practice: The market is busy on Saturday.
We walk to the market in the morning.
Apples are cheap at the market.
The café is behind the market.
words.tutor: Tell the tutor three things you get at a made-up market. Give each price as a number only, like The apples are 2.

words.meaning: A big building with doctors and nurses.
words.example: My aunt is a nurse at the hospital.
practice: The hospital is on the corner.
Take the number 5 bus to the hospital.
A doctor works at the hospital.
Where is the hospital, please?
words.tutor: Say hos-pi-tal in three parts, then as one word. Ask the tutor to check that HOS is the strong part.

words.meaning: A place with many books. You can borrow them.
words.example: I borrow books from the library.
practice: The library is next to the school.
Is the library open on Sunday?
She reads at the library in the afternoon.
I walk to the library with my friend.
words.tutor: Ask the tutor what a person can do at a library. Answer with three lines: I can borrow …, I can read …, I can …

words.meaning: A shop. You get medicine and soap there.
words.example: I get soap at the chemist.
practice: The chemist is between the bank and the café.
Is there a chemist on this street?
The chemist opens at eight o'clock.
Go to the chemist on the corner.
words.tutor: Chemist starts like key. Say chemist to the tutor five times, and ask it to check the start each time.

words.meaning: A place. You send a letter or a box from here.
words.example: I send a letter at the post office.
practice: The post office is behind the bank.
Is the post office open today?
Walk to the corner. The post office is there.
She works at the post office.
words.tutor: Ask the tutor to be the person at a post office desk. Say what you want to send, a letter or a box, and answer its questions.

words.meaning: A small place. You drink tea or coffee there, and eat.
words.example: We have coffee at the café.
practice: The café is in front of the park.
Is there a café near the station?
I meet my friend at the café.
The tea at the café is cheap.
words.tutor: Ask the tutor for a made-up café list with three drinks and their prices. Ask for one with Can I have …, please?

words.meaning: A place. You see a film there with a lot of people.
words.example: We see a film at the cinema on Saturday.
practice: The cinema is behind the market.
Is the cinema near here?
The film at the cinema is at seven o'clock.
I go to the cinema with my cousin.
words.tutor: Cinema starts like city. Say city, then cinema, to the tutor. Ask it to check the start of cinema.

words.meaning: A house, a school, a bank: each one is a building.
words.example: The bank is a big white building.
practice: The hospital is a tall building.
There are four buildings on my street.
The café is in an old building.
Which building is the library?
words.tutor: Describe a made-up building to the tutor with a colour and a size, like a tall grey building. Ask it to guess what is in the building.

words.meaning: The place where two streets meet.
words.example: The chemist is on the corner.
practice: Walk to the corner.
The café on the corner is new.
Wait at the corner.
There is a bin in the corner of the room.
words.tutor: On the corner: a street. In the corner: a room. Say one line of each to the tutor and ask it to check the small word.

words.meaning: You wash with it and water. It makes things clean.
words.example: I wash my hands with soap.
practice: The soap is next to the towel.
Wash the cups with soap and water.
Can I have the soap, please?
There is no soap in the kitchen.
words.tutor: Say three lines with soap to the tutor, like some soap or no soap. Ask it to check you did not say a soap.

words.meaning: A soft thing. Your hands are wet, and it makes them dry.
words.example: I dry my hands with a towel.
practice: The towel is behind the door.
This towel is wet.
Can I have a clean towel, please?
There are two towels on the shelf.
words.tutor: Tell the tutor where a made-up towel is, with behind, on or next to. Ask it to check the place word.

words.meaning: A tool. You move it on the floor, and it cleans.
words.example: I clean the floor with a brush.
practice: The brush is in the kitchen.
Can I borrow your brush?
This brush is old and dirty.
Clean the table with this brush.
words.starter: I clean the … with a brush.
words.tutor: Ask the tutor for three jobs in a room. Say which one you do with a brush, in a whole line: I clean the floor with a brush.

words.meaning: A thing in your hand. It helps you make or fix things.
words.example: He fixes the chair with a tool.
practice: A knife is a tool.
Put the tools in the box.
Which tool do you use?
This tool is for you. It is a present.
words.tutor: Name a job, like fix a bike or cut bread. Ask the tutor which tool you use, then say it: I fix it with …

words.meaning: A small tool with two long parts. You cut paper with it.
words.example: I cut the paper with scissors.
practice: The scissors are on the desk.
Can I borrow your scissors?
These scissors are new.
Cut the card with the scissors.
words.tutor: Scissors is one thing, but it goes with are. Say three lines about scissors and ask the tutor to check you said are.

words.meaning: A thing you give to a person. You say: This is for you.
words.example: This present is for you.
practice: I have got a present for my sister.
The present is in a small box.
Who is the present for?
I got a present from my aunt.
words.tutor: Make up a present for three people. Tell the tutor who gets each one, with for: The book is for my cousin.

grammar.title: Behind, between, in front of, to
grammar.explanation:
Say where a person or a place is.
Dan is between Eva and Zoe.
Say where you go. Use to.
I walk to the café.
grammar.rule:
Three people at a bus stop:
Eva, then Dan, then Zoe.

in front of: Eva is in front of Dan.
behind: Zoe is behind Dan.
between: Dan is between Eva and Zoe.

A street: bank, café, chemist.
The café is between the bank and the chemist.
A taxi is in front of the café.
The cinema is behind the café.

to: where you go
I walk to the corner.
She goes to the library.

to: you are going.  at: you are there.
I go to the bank. Now I am at the bank.
grammar.workedExample:
The café is ___ the bank and the chemist.
1. Look: two places, the bank and the chemist.
2. The café has one place on each side.
3. One on each side: between.
4. Write: The café is between the bank and the chemist.
5. Check: between, then two places with and. Yes.
grammar.mistake:
It is easy to leave out of.
No: The bus is in front the bank.
Yes: The bus is in front of the bank.
In front of is three words.
No: I go at the bank.
Yes: I go to the bank.
grammar.tip: In front of: three words. Between: two things.
grammar.practice:
Eva, Dan and Zoe are at a bus stop. Eva is first, Dan is second, Zoe is third.
Write behind, between, in front of or to.
1. Eva is ___ Dan.
2. Zoe is ___ Dan.
3. Dan is ___ Eva and Zoe.
4. In the morning, Dan walks ___ the station.
5. The bus is first, and the car is second. The car is ___ the bus.
6. I walk ___ the post office.
7. The chemist is ___ the bank and the café.
grammar.answers:
1. in front of  2. behind  3. between  4. to  5. behind  6. to  7. between
Wrong on 1 or 2? Eva is first, so she is in front. Zoe is last, so she is behind.
Wrong on 4 or 6? The person is going there: to, not at.

grammar.title: With a knife: the tool you use
grammar.explanation:
With can say what you use.
I cut the bread with a knife.
For says who gets it.
The bread is for you.
grammar.rule:
with: the thing you use
I cut the bread with a knife.
I wash my hands with soap.
I dry my hands with a towel.
I clean the floor with a brush.
He fixes the bike with a tool.

for: the person who gets it
This present is for you.
I make a card for my sister.

You use it: with.  A person gets it: for.

With a friend: together.
With a knife: you use it.

Scissors is one thing, but say are:
The scissors are on the desk.
grammar.workedExample:
I cut the paper ___ scissors. It is a card ___ my aunt.
1. Scissors: I use them. I cut with them.
2. The thing I use: with.
3. My aunt gets the card.
4. The person who gets it: for.
5. Write: I cut the paper with scissors. It is a card for my aunt.
grammar.mistake:
It is easy to say for in place of with.
No: I cut the bread for a knife.
Yes: I cut the bread with a knife.
The knife does not get the bread. You use it.
grammar.tip: You use it: with. A person gets it: for.
grammar.practice:
Write with or for.
1. I wash the cups ___ soap.
2. This present is ___ you.
3. She cuts the card ___ scissors.
4. I dry my hands ___ a towel.
5. The tea is ___ my grandmother.
6. He cleans the floor ___ a brush.
7. I walk to the park ___ a friend.
grammar.answers:
1. with  2. for  3. with  4. with  5. for  6. with  7. with
Wrong on 2 or 5? A person gets it: for.
Number 7: with a friend is together. That is with too.

grammar.title: I'm tired. I feel happy.
grammar.explanation:
Say how you feel.
Use I'm and a feeling word.
Or use I feel.
I'm tired. I feel happy.
grammar.rule:
I'm and a feeling
I'm tired.
I'm hungry.
She is worried.
They are cold.

I feel and a feeling
I feel happy.
He feels sad.
We feel tired.

Ask: How do you feel? How are you?
Say no: I'm not hungry. I don't feel cold.

afraid of: She is afraid of the water.
grammar.workedExample:
Dan didn't eat today. How does he feel?
1. He didn't eat. He wants to eat.
2. He wants to eat: hungry.
3. Dan is one man: he. He goes with is.
4. Write: He is hungry.
5. Or: He feels hungry. For he, say feels.
grammar.mistake:
Use I'm or I feel. Not both.
No: I'm feel tired.
Yes: I feel tired. Or: I'm tired.
No: I have hungry.
Yes: I'm hungry.
grammar.tip: I'm tired. I feel tired. Not: I'm feel tired.
grammar.practice:
Write a feeling word: happy, sad, tired, hungry, thirsty, angry, worried, afraid, cold.
1. I want to sleep. I'm ___.
2. I want to drink. I'm ___.
3. I didn't eat today. I'm ___.
4. It is Saturday, and my friends are here. I feel ___.
5. The window is open, and it is not hot. I'm ___.
6. It is eleven at night. My sister is not here. I'm ___.
7. I'm in the water, and I can't swim. I'm ___.
8. Write it right: I'm feel sad.
grammar.answers:
1. tired  2. thirsty  3. hungry  4. happy  5. cold  6. worried  7. afraid
8. I feel sad. Or: I'm sad.
Wrong on 8? Use I'm or I feel, not both.
Number 6: worried is when a bad thing can happen.

readings.title: A Busy Saturday
readings.setting: A market, a café and a post office in a town, on one Saturday.
readings.passage:
It is Saturday. My name is Tomas.
In the morning, I walk to the market.
I get fruit and fish for my mother.
The café is between the market and the bank.
I'm thirsty, and I have a cup of tea there.
Then I go to the post office with a box.
There are ten people in front of me.
My neighbour Dan is behind me.
The post office closes at twelve o'clock.
I'm tired, and I'm worried.
At twelve, the man at the desk takes my box.
It is a present for my cousin.
Now I feel happy.

readings.title: Where Do You Go?
readings.setting: Places in a town, and what you do there.
readings.passage:
Where do you go in a town?
A book to borrow? Go to the library.
A letter or a box to send? Go to the post office.
Hungry or thirsty? Go to a café.
Soap or medicine? Go to the chemist.
Fruit, fish and vegetables? Go to the market.
A new film? Go to the cinema.
Money? Go to the bank.
Doctors and nurses work at the hospital.
Many towns have a market in front of the station.
You can find a café on a corner.

readings.title: A Note on the Post Office Door
readings.setting: The door of a post office in a town.
readings.passage:
POST OFFICE
Closed on Saturday.

On Saturday, please go to the post office in the market.
Walk to the corner.
The market is in front of the station.
The post office is between the café and the bank.
It opens at 9 and closes at 12.

Letters and boxes: go to desk 1.
Please wait behind the yellow line.

comprehension.a: Between the market and the bank.
comprehension.why: Line 4: The café is between the market and the bank.

comprehension.q: What does Tomas have at the café?
comprehension.why: Line 5: I'm thirsty, and I have a cup of tea there.

comprehension.q: There are ten people in front of Tomas. Is he first at the desk?
comprehension.a: No. Ten people are in front of him.
comprehension.why: Line 7: There are ten people in front of me. In front of him: they go first.

comprehension.a: Ten people are in front of him. It closes at twelve.
comprehension.why:
Line 7: ten people are in front of him.
Line 9: the post office closes at twelve.
Line 12: It is a present for my cousin. For: the person who gets it.

comprehension.q: You have a letter to send. Where do you go?
comprehension.why: Line 3: A letter or a box to send? Go to the post office.

comprehension.q: Where can you borrow a book?
comprehension.why: Line 2: A book to borrow? Go to the library.

comprehension.q: It is Saturday. You have a box to send. Where do you go?
comprehension.a: To the post office in the market. It is between the café and the bank.
comprehension.why:
The note says: please go to the post office in the market.
It is between the café and the bank.

comprehension.q: It is Saturday, at one o'clock. Can you send a letter there?
comprehension.why: The note says: It opens at 9 and closes at 12. One o'clock is after 12.

comprehension.q: Please wait behind the yellow line. Where is the line?
comprehension.a: In front of you. You wait behind it.
comprehension.why: Behind the line: the line is in front of you. Do not stand on it.

speaking.title: Speaking 1 — In front of, behind, between
speaking.instructions:
Listen. Say each line.
Eva, Dan and Zoe are at a bus stop.
Eva is in front of Dan.
Zoe is behind Dan.
Dan is between Eva and Zoe.
The café is between the bank and the chemist.
I walk to the corner.
Tap the mic. Say the 6 lines.
Tap the mic again. Listen.
Check: in front of, all three words?
Between: two names, like Eva and Zoe?
To in the last line?
speaking.tutor: Ask the tutor to name three people at a bus stop, in order. Say where each one is, with in front of, behind or between.

speaking.title: Speaking 2 — Where is the chemist?
speaking.instructions:
You are on a street in a town. You ask the way.
Listen. Say your lines.
You: Hello. Where is the chemist, please?
Person: Walk to the corner.
Person: The chemist is between the bank and the café.
You: Between the bank and the café?
Person: Yes. It is in front of the bus stop.
You: Thanks! Is there a post office near here?
Person: Yes. It is behind the bank.
You: Behind the bank. Thanks. Goodbye!
Tap the mic. Say your lines. Tap again. Listen.
Check: please in your question?
Did you say each place back, to check it?
Thanks at the end?
A friend can read the person's lines. No one with you? Read them and answer.
speaking.tutor: Ask the tutor to be a person on a made-up street. Ask where two places are, and say each answer back to check it.

speaking.title: Speaking 3 — With a knife, for a friend
speaking.instructions:
Listen. Say each line.
I cut the bread with a knife.
I wash my hands with soap.
I dry my hands with a towel.
I clean the floor with a brush.
I cut the paper with scissors.
The card is for my friend.
Now answer. Say a whole line.
What do you cut bread with?
What do you wash your hands with?
Who is the card for?
Tap the mic. Say the 6 lines and the 3 answers. Tap again. Listen.
Check with these:
I cut bread with a knife.
I wash my hands with soap.
The card is for my friend.
With before a knife and soap? For before my friend?
speaking.tutor: Ask the tutor to name a job, like wash the cups. Say what you do it with, in a whole line: I wash the cups with soap.

speaking.title: Speaking 4 — Listen: work out the new word
speaking.instructions:
Tap Listen. Do not read. Listen two times.
Hello. I'm Lena. I work at the library.
Walk to the corner. You can see the park.
The library is opposite the park.
It is on the other side of the street.
At the desk, there is a queue.
Please wait in the queue, behind the other people.
The library has a new café.
You can have tea and a sandwich there.
Now answer. Tap the mic. Say each answer.
1. The library is opposite the park. Where is it? A: in the park. B: on the other side of the street. C: behind the park.
2. What is a queue? A: people in a line, waiting. B: a desk. C: a book.
3. What is a sandwich? A: a drink. B: bread with meat or egg in it. C: a film.
4. Where does Lena work?
Tap again. Listen to your answers.
Check: 1 B. 2 A. 3 B. 4 At the library.
A new word? Listen to the words around it.
Opposite: on the other side of the street.
Queue: you wait in it, behind other people.
Sandwich: you have it with tea. It is a thing to eat.
speaking.tutor: Ask the tutor to say one line about a café or a shop, with one word you do not know. Say what you think the word means, then ask if you are right.

speaking.title: Speaking 5 — A made-up day: how does Eva feel?
speaking.instructions:
Here is a made-up day. It is about Eva, not about you.
Read each line. Say how Eva feels.
1. At 7 o'clock, Eva wants to sleep.
2. At 1 o'clock, she didn't eat.
3. At 3 o'clock, her bus is late. Her train is at 4.
4. At 6 o'clock, a friend gives her a present.
5. At 9 o'clock, the window is open. It is not hot.
Tap the mic. Say 5 lines: She is … or She feels …
Now say them as Eva: I'm … or I feel …
Tap again. Listen.
Check with these:
1. She is tired.
2. She is hungry.
3. She is worried.
4. She feels happy.
5. She feels cold.
I'm or I feel in each Eva line? Not I'm feel?
speaking.tutor: Ask the tutor for a made-up day with five times in it. For each time, say how the person feels, with is or feels.

speaking.title: Speaking 6 — Say the town words
speaking.instructions:
Listen and repeat.
bank, market, corner
HOS-pi-tal, hospital
Chemist starts like key: chemist
Cinema starts like city: cinema
library, post office, café, building
Now say these lines.
The bank is on the corner.
The library is between the café and the cinema.
The hospital is a tall building.
I walk to the post office.
The chemist is behind the market.
Tap the mic. Say the 10 words and the 5 lines. Tap again. Listen.
Check: chemist starts like key?
HOS strong in hospital?
In front of, behind or between: all the words?
speaking.tutor: Say the ten town words to the tutor in any order. Ask it which one was hard to hear, and say that word again three times.

writing.title: Writing 1 — A street in a town
writing.prompt:
Write 5 lines about a street in a town.
Say where the places are.
Use behind, between and in front of.
It can be a made-up street.
writing.model:
This is Station Street.
The bank is on the corner.
The café is between the bank and the chemist.
A bus stop is in front of the café.
The cinema is behind the café.
writing.criteria:
5 sentences.
Behind, between and in front of: one each, at least.
Between: two places with and.
A capital letter and a full stop in each.
writing.support:
Copy the model.
Change one place in each line.
Keep the words behind, between and in front of.
writing.extension: Add a line with to: I walk to the bank.

writing.title: Writing 2 — What do you use?
writing.prompt:
Write 4 lines about jobs in a room.
Say what you use, with with.
Then write 1 line about a present, with for.
It can be made up.
writing.model:
I wash the cups with soap.
I dry my hands with a towel.
I clean the floor with a brush.
I cut the bread with a knife.
This card is for my friend.
writing.criteria:
5 sentences.
With and a thing in lines 1 to 4.
For and a person in line 5.
A capital letter and a full stop in each.
writing.support:
Match first: wash, soap. Dry, towel. Clean, brush. Cut, knife.
Write each pair in a line: I wash the cups with soap.
writing.extension: Add a line with scissors: I cut the paper with scissors.

writing.title: Writing 3 — A made-up day: how I feel
writing.prompt:
Write about a made-up day.
Write 5 lines. Give a time and a feeling in each line.
Use I'm or I feel.
writing.model:
At 7 o'clock, I'm tired.
At 8 o'clock, I walk to work or to school. I'm cold.
At 1 o'clock, I'm hungry, and I eat at a café.
At 4 o'clock, my bus is late. I'm worried.
At 8 o'clock, my friend calls. I feel happy.
writing.criteria:
5 lines.
A time in each line: at 7 o'clock.
A feeling word in each line.
I'm or I feel. Not I'm feel.
One line with and in the middle.
A capital letter and a full stop in each.
writing.support:
Copy the model.
Change only the feeling words.
Use the list: happy, sad, tired, hungry, thirsty, angry, worried, afraid, cold.
writing.extension: Add a line about a friend: At 6 o'clock, my friend is tired.

writing.title: Writing 4 — A note: how to go
writing.prompt:
A friend is coming to a café in your town.
Write a note like Reading 3.
Say where to walk. Say where the café is.
It can be a made-up town.
writing.model:
Hello, Dan!
The café is on Green Street.
Walk to the corner.
The café is between the bank and the library.
It is in front of the bus stop.
I'm at the café at 3 o'clock.
writing.criteria:
5 or 6 lines.
Walk to or go to in one line.
Between, behind or in front of in two lines.
A time with at.
A capital letter and a full stop in each.
writing.support:
Copy the model.
Change the name and the places.
Check the place words in Reading 3.
writing.extension: Add a line: Please wait in front of the café.

activities.title: Practice 1 — Behind, between, in front of
activities.instructions:
Read. Then write behind, between or in front of.
Five people are at a bus stop, in this order:
Eva, Dan, Zoe, Tomas, Lena.
1. Eva is ___ Dan.
2. Dan is ___ Eva and Zoe.
3. Lena is ___ Tomas.
4. Tomas is ___ Zoe and Lena.
5. Zoe is ___ Tomas.
Park Street has three places: a bank, a café and a chemist.
6. The café is ___ the bank and the chemist.
7. A taxi stops at the café door. The taxi is ___ the café.
8. The cinema is at the back of the café. You cannot see it from the street. The cinema is ___ the café.
activities.answers:
1. in front of  2. between  3. behind  4. between  5. in front of  6. between  7. in front of  8. behind
Wrong on 2, 4 or 6? One on each side: between. Write the two with and.
Wrong on 1 or 5? Before the other person in the line: in front of.
7 or 8 right: good.
6 or less: read Pattern 1 and do it again.
activities.solo: Draw five people in a line, and write their names. Then write your answers and check with the key.

activities.title: Practice 2 — Go to, be at
activities.instructions:
Write to or at.
1. I walk ___ the library.
2. Now I am ___ the library.
3. She goes ___ the bank on Monday.
4. He works ___ the hospital.
5. We take a taxi ___ the station.
6. Wait ___ the corner.
7. They go ___ the cinema on Saturday.
8. I meet my friend ___ the café.
activities.answers:
1. to  2. at  3. to  4. at  5. to  6. at  7. to  8. at
Walk, go, take a taxi: you are going there. Use to.
Am, work, wait, meet: you are there. Use at.
7 or 8 right: good.
6 or less: read Pattern 1 and do it again.
activities.solo: Say each line out loud. Ask: going there, or there now? Write to or at. Check with the key.

activities.title: Practice 3 — With or for
activities.instructions:
Write with or for.
1. I cut the bread ___ a knife.
2. This tea is ___ you.
3. I clean the desk ___ a brush.
4. The present is ___ my brother.
5. She dries her hands ___ a towel.
6. I have got a card ___ my grandmother.
7. He fixes the chair ___ a tool.
8. I cut the paper ___ scissors.
activities.answers:
1. with  2. for  3. with  4. for  5. with  6. for  7. with  8. with
Wrong on 2, 4 or 6? A person gets the thing: for.
Wrong on 1, 3, 5, 7 or 8? You use the thing: with.
7 or 8 right: good.
6 or less: read Pattern 2 and do it again.
activities.solo:
Ask: do I use it? Or does a person get it?
Write your answer. Check with the key.

activities.title: Practice 4 — Which thing do you use?
activities.instructions:
Match 1 to 6 with a to f.
1. I wash my hands with …
2. I dry my hands with …
3. I cut the paper with …
4. I clean the floor with …
5. I fix the bike with …
6. I cut the meat with …
a. a brush.
b. scissors.
c. soap.
d. a tool.
e. a knife.
f. a towel.
activities.answers:
1c  2f  3b  4a  5d  6e
Numbers 3 and 6: scissors and a knife both cut. Paper: scissors. Meat: a knife.
5 or 6 right: good.
4 or less: go back to Words, Things you use.
activities.solo: Read each line out loud with its end. Write the letter. Check with the key.

activities.title: Practice 5 — How do they feel?
activities.instructions:
Write a feeling word: happy, sad, tired, hungry, thirsty, angry, worried, afraid, cold.
1. The farmer worked all day. He wants to sleep. He is ___.
2. The nurse wants a glass of water. She is ___.
3. My cousin lost his phone. He is ___.
4. It is Sunday, and my family is here. I feel ___.
5. A man took my neighbour's bike! My neighbour is ___.
6. It is eleven at night. My sister is not here. I'm ___.
7. The boy can't swim. He is ___ of the water.
8. The window is open, and the room is not hot. I feel ___.
activities.answers:
1. tired  2. thirsty  3. sad (worried is right too)  4. happy  5. angry  6. worried  7. afraid  8. cold
Number 7: afraid comes with of.
7 or 8 right: good.
6 or less: read Pattern 3 and do it again.
activities.solo: Read each line. Ask: what does the person want, or what happened? Write the word. Check with the key.

activities.title: Practice 6 — Follow the sign
activities.instructions:
Read the sign. Do what it says. Then answer.
SIGN AT THE STATION
To the library:
1. Walk to the corner.
2. Go to the big market.
3. The library is behind the market.
4. It is between the cinema and the café.
5. Please use the green door.
Questions.
1. Where do you walk first?
2. Where is the library: in front of the market, or behind it?
3. What is on each side of the library?
4. Which door do you use?
5. You are in front of the market. Can you see the library well?
activities.answers:
1. To the corner.  2. Behind the market.  3. The cinema and the café.  4. The green door.  5. No. The market is in front of it.
4 or 5 right: good.
3 or less: read the sign again.
Read one line at a time, and point.
activities.solo:
Draw a small map of the sign.
The corner, then the market, then the library behind it.
Answer the questions. Check with the key.

quizzes.q: Eva is first in the line. Dan is second. Eva is ___ Dan.
quizzes.why: First in the line: in front of. Behind is the other way: Dan is behind Eva. Between needs two people, one on each side. To says where you go.

quizzes.q: The café is ___ the bank and the chemist.
quizzes.why: One place on each side, with and: between. In front needs of after it. Behind has no of after it. To says where you go.

options: The bus is in front the bank.
The bus is in front to the bank.
The bus in front of the bank.
The bus is in front of the bank.
quizzes.a: The bus is in front of the bank.
quizzes.why: In front of is three words, and the line needs is. Line 1 has no of. Line 2 has to, not of. Line 3 has no is.
Walk: you are going there, so to. At: you are there. I am at the post office. In: inside a thing. With: a person, or a thing you use.

quizzes.q: You have a letter to send. Where do you go?
quizzes.why: You send letters and boxes at the post office. At the cinema you see a film. At the library you borrow books. At the market you get fruit and fish.

quizzes.q: I cut the bread ___ a knife.
quizzes.why: You use the knife, so with. For: the person who gets the bread. To and at: places.
My sister gets the present, so for. With: a thing you use, or a friend with you. At: a place. Behind: a place word.

quizzes.q: Your hands are wet. What do you use?
quizzes.why: A towel makes wet hands dry. You wash with soap, and then your hands are wet again. Scissors cut. A brush cleans a floor.
Use I feel or I'm, not both. I'm feel has both. We do not say I have tired: say I'm tired. I tired has no am and no feel.

quizzes.q: Tomas didn't eat today. He is ___.
quizzes.why: He didn't eat, so he wants to eat: hungry. Thirsty is when you want to drink. Tired is when you want to sleep. Cold is when you are not hot.

quizzes.q: At the market, there is a long queue. You wait at the end of it, behind a man. What is a queue?
quizzes.why: You wait behind a man, at the end. It is a line of people. A shop and a building have no end to wait at. A price is a number.

quizzes.q: A sign says: Please wait behind the yellow line. Where do you stand?
quizzes.why: The sign says behind, so the line is in front of you. In front of the line is the wrong side. On the line is not behind it. There is one line, not two.

teacherNotes.note: Every card shows one item done before its practice, every exercise has a key with a score line, and every speaking task ends with record, listen back and a checklist. The listening task, Speaking 4, asks the learner to listen before reading and to work out three new words (opposite, queue, sandwich) from the words around them. Those three are deduced, not taught, so do not test their spelling. If you are helping, read the talk aloud as a second voice and let the learner answer before either of you looks at the key.

Dropping of from in front of (in front the bank), at for a direction (I go at the bank), and using both I'm and feel (I'm feel tired). I have hungry is also common; show I'm hungry and move on. Point at the word that is missing or extra rather than giving the whole answer; the keys explain each one.

Cambridge asks for basic feelings, with support. Every task here puts the feeling on a person in a text or on a made-up day, and none asks how the learner really feels or why. Keep it that way. Cold means the feeling of cold only; I have a cold is not taught. The hospital and the chemist appear as places in a town, never as advice about health.

Was, were and felt belong to a later unit, so feelings are always in the present: I'm tired, she feels happy. Directions use walk to, go to and the place words only; turn left and turn right are not taught yet. In the patterns, texts and practice, for means only the person who gets a thing, so they avoid go to the café for a coffee and wait for. With keeps its Unit 6 meaning (with a friend) beside the new one (with a knife), and Pattern 2 shows the two together.

The AI tutor is a rehearsal partner, not a marking service, and no task is scored by it alone. Tasks say that made-up streets, towns and days are fine. Never ask a learner to name their real street, their bank or a hospital they have used.

selfAssessment.statement: I can say: The café is between the bank and the chemist.
I can ask the way, and say: Walk to the corner.
I can write: I cut it with a knife. It is for you.
I can say how a person feels: She is tired.
I can write how people feel on a made-up day.
I can work out a new word from the words around it.
I can read a notice and do what it says.

assignment.title: Where things go
assignment.instructions:
Two parts.
1. Tap the mic. Say 4 lines about a street: where 3 places are, and where you walk. Then say 2 lines about a made-up day: how a person feels.
2. Write a note like Writing 4: how to go to a café. Add one line with with: I cut it with scissors.
Add one line with for: It is for you.
You can make up the town, the people and the day.
assignment.submissionType: Audio recording and a written note
